primary.thesis: The ladder brackets ETH roughly between $1,000 and $3,000, and the $2,000 up-rung was clearly added later with its own 'from creation' rule. That suggests ETH was trading in the high-$1,000s to around $2,000 when the market was set up. On June 16 only about two weeks of the month are left, so the outermost rungs on both sides need a move of roughly 40-50% or more in that time. ETH can move that much, but it usually takes a big shock such as an exchange failure, a stablecoin depeg or a major regulatory surprise. Without one, touch contracts at the far ends of the ladder tend to expire NO. The thesis is that ETH stays inside a wide middle band ($1,200-$2,800) for the rest of June, so the far-tail rungs on both sides resolve NO.

basket.reason: $3,000 is the top rung and needs roughly a 50%+ rally in about two weeks from a level near or below $2,000. It is the most remote upside touch on the ladder.
$2,800 still needs a rally of roughly 40%+ in the second half of the month. That would take a regime change such as an ETF, macro or regulatory catalyst, not ordinary volatility.
$1,000 is the bottom rung. Reaching it requires a crash of roughly half the price, which needs a systemic crypto failure (a big exchange, a stablecoin or a cascade of forced selling).
$1,100 is only slightly less remote than $1,000. It needs the same kind of systemic liquidation event within the remaining weeks.

failure_narrative: The basket loses only if ETH has an extreme move in the second half of June. On the downside, a crypto-specific or macro shock could set off a forced-selling cascade: a major exchange or lender becomes insolvent, USDT loses its peg, a large leveraged holder such as a corporate ETH treasury is forced to sell, or a sharp global risk-off move drains liquidity. Any of these could push a Binance 1-minute low under $1,100 or $1,000. A brief liquidation wick that lasts one minute is enough, because the contract counts touches, not closes. On the upside, a sudden catalyst could drive a violent short squeeze through $2,800 or $3,000, for example a surprise approval or regulatory ruling, or a large institutional buying program. The common thread is a volatility regime shift, in which ETH's realized volatility over two weeks becomes several times its normal level.
hedge_thesis: The primary fails in worlds where crypto volatility explodes. The downside version is the more plausible one. In those worlds the stress is rarely confined to ETH. It shows up in Bitcoin drawdowns, falling crypto-exposed equities (Coinbase, Strategy/MicroStrategy, miners), stress on stablecoin pegs such as Tether trading below $1, and often a wider risk-off move with the VIX rising and Nasdaq falling. The mechanism is shared: leverage and collateral links between ETH, BTC, stablecoins and crypto-treasury companies. A forced liquidation or a counterparty failure in one of them spreads through margin calls to the others. So contracts on BTC falling below its downside thresholds, on crypto equities dropping, on a Tether depeg or on a VIX spike would tend to pay off exactly when ETH breaks through its far-tail rungs.
